title: Quantitative GC–MS Method for Detection of ∆9-THC and THC—COOH in Postmortem Samples
author: Paknahad, Jokar, et al.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare stock solutions of 1 mg/mL Δ9‑THC in methanol for blood and THC‑COOH in methanol for urine; make working solutions of 100, 1000 and 10 000 ng/mL in methanol; then prepare urine calibrators at 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250 and 300 ng/mL and blood calibrators at 15, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200 and 300 ng/mL using drug‑free matrices.

steps.title: Prepare control standards
steps.instruction: Prepare control solutions containing THC‑COOH (urine) and Δ9‑THC (blood) at 100 ng/mL and 1000 ng/mL respectively; additionally, for urine make control levels of THC‑COOH at 85, 125 and 225 ng/mL in drug‑free urine, and for blood make control levels of Δ9‑THC at 25, 180 and 250 ng/mL in drug‑free blood.

steps.title: Process urine samples
steps.instruction: For each urine calibrator, add 1 mL drug‑free urine and 50 µL CBN internal standard (100 ng/mL) to a 16 × 100 mm screw‑cap glass tube; add 200 µL of 11.8 N KOH, incubate at 80 °C for 30 min, cool to room temperature, then add 2 mL 0.1 M acetic acid, 200 µL glacial acetic acid and 5 mL extraction solvent (n‑hexane/ethyl acetate 8:2 v/v); shake vigorously 5 min, centrifuge at 1800 × g for 7 min, transfer the organic layer to a 1.5 mL GC‑MS vial, dry under N₂ at 50 °C, add 50 µL MSTFA and incubate at 70 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Process blood samples
steps.instruction: Mix 50 µL internal‑standard solution with 1 mL blood; vortex and perform liquid‑liquid extraction for 5 min with 5 mL n‑hexane/ethyl acetate (9:1 v/v); centrifuge at 2800 × g, collect the organic phase, acidify the remaining aqueous phase to pH 4–5 with 100 µL 1 M HCl and repeat the extraction; centrifuge again, combine organic extracts, dry completely under N₂ at 50 °C, add 50 µL MSTFA and silylate in an oven pre‑heated to 80 °C for 30 min, then inject 0.6 µL of the derivatized sample into the GC‑MS splitless inlet at 280 °C.

steps.title: Set up GC‑MS instrument
steps.instruction: Install an Agilent HP‑5MS capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film, Macherey‑Nagel); set helium carrier gas flow to 1.2 mL/min (blood method notes 1.3 mL/min); configure injector temperature to 250 °C (urine) and 280 °C (blood) in splitless mode; set MS electron‑ionization at 70 eV, use SIM mode with the ion lists provided; apply a solvent delay of 3 min, injection volume 0.5 µL (blood injection uses 0.6 µL); set detector temperature to 280 °C; program oven temperature: initial 120 °C (hold 0.5 min), ramp 30 °C/min to final 6 min (urine) or follow blood program – Ramp 1: 70 °C for 2 min, Ramp 2: 20 °C/min to 250 °C (hold 4 min), Ramp 3: 20 °C/min to 300 °C (hold 17 min); set MS source temperature to 230 °C.

description: The GC–MS technique was validated in accordance with current standards [18,19]. This methodology supports pharmacokinetic studies and concentration monitoring of known analytes (i.e., dose) and their metabolites. Interferences were assessed in accordance with SWGTOX criteria.
